title: Music and musical instruments
subtitle: play the guitar, a musician, classical music
summary: Use music, musical and musician correctly, name musical instruments and say what kind of music you like.

lesson.heading: music, musical and musician
lesson.text: **Music** is an uncountable noun, so it has no plural. **Musical** is an adjective. A **musician** is a person who plays music.

examples.text: The band played fantastic **music** for more than two hours.
There is a shop on King Street that sells **musical instruments**.
My brother is a very good **musician**. He plays three instruments.

lesson.heading: Musical instruments
rows: you press the black and white keys
you hold it and play the strings with your fingers
a small instrument with strings, played under your chin
a big instrument with strings, played sitting down
a metal instrument you hold across your mouth and blow
a long black instrument you blow
a gold instrument you blow, with three buttons
lesson.note: We always say play the piano, play the guitar - with the.

lesson.heading: Playing an instrument
lesson.text: You **play the** guitar, you are **learning the** guitar, or you **have** guitar **lessons**. A person who plays the flute is a **flute-player**; a person who plays the violin is a **violinist** and a person who plays the piano is a **pianist**.

examples.text: Ava **plays the clarinet**. Her brother **plays the drums**.
Krishnan is **learning the guitar**. His friend Isabella **has piano lessons**.
Mia is a very good **flute-player**. She plays in an **orchestra**.
Lucas is an excellent **violinist**. His sister is a good **pianist**.

lesson.heading: Kinds of music
lesson.text: **Classical** music means Beethoven and Mozart. Other kinds are **pop**, **folk**, **jazz**, **rock** and **opera**. If you really dislike something, you **can't stand** it.

examples.text: Harper **can't stand opera**. She prefers **pop music**.

lesson.heading: band and concert
lesson.text: A **band** is a group of musicians. A **concert** is an event with music. Do not add the word *music* to either of them.

examples.text: Nuala had a really good **band** at her 21st birthday party.

lesson.text: Say I listen to music, never ~~I listen music~~.

exercises.prompt: What are your favourite types of ___?
exercises.explanation: Music is the noun for the sound itself.

exercises.prompt: My brother thinks he's a good ___, but he's very bad!
exercises.explanation: A musician is a person who plays music.
Musical is the adjective: a musical instrument.

exercises.prompt: I love ___ music. Beethoven is my favourite.
exercises.explanation: The word is classical music, not classic music.

exercises.prompt: My brother ___ folk music, but I love it.
exercises.explanation: Can't stand means dislike something very much.

exercises.prompt: I have some tickets for a ___ at the Town Hall. Would you like one?
exercises.explanation: A concert already means an event with music.

exercises.prompt: I always ___ music when I'm studying.
exercises.explanation: Listen always takes to before the thing you hear.

exercises.prompt: My sister plays in a ___ with three other girls from her school.
exercises.explanation: A band is a group of musicians.

exercises.prompt: Match the description with the word.

pairs.left: a person who plays the violin
a person who plays the piano

exercises.prompt: Noah loves playing the ___. He hits them with two sticks.
exercises.explanation: You play the drums with sticks.

exercises.statement: The band played fantastic musics for more than two hours.
exercises.explanation: The band played fantastic music for more than two hours. Music is uncountable and has no plural.
